angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 732,572 km at 45.60 pc = 0.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.9301 +/- 0.0267 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 45.60 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.053 +/- 0.026 solar radii from Teske et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 86226 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160...96T/abstract): 732,572 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.019 +/- 0.061 solar masses from Teske et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 86226 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160...96T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5863 +/- 88 K from Teske et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 86226 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160...96T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Teske et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 86226 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160...96T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-86226.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.401, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
